title: Starry night at Paranal
caption: Star trails over the Very Large Telescope, Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: Through a night at ESO's Very Large Telescope (VLT), the stars appear to wheel around the southern celestial pole. On the right, one of the observatory's four 8.2-metre telescopes goes about its nightly job of studying the heavens, and two of the four 1.8-metre Auxiliary Telescopes also appear in the frame.

The observatory stands on Cerro Paranal in Chile's dry Atacama Desert, 2600 metres above sea level, and its skies give the astronomers below splendid chances to observe. That high, dry setting, together with extraordinarily advanced equipment, makes time on the VLT highly prized by astronomers around the world.
The circular paths are an effect of Earth's rotation. The stars only appear to move because our planet turns, and a camera recording over time turns that motion into trails.

understand.summary: This is a star-trail photograph by Iztok Bončina, recording the sky's apparent motion over time. The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The trails build up only because the camera recorded Earth's rotation.
